segments.label: zai-five-hour-window · cc:-home-joe · said 2026-10-12
segments.text:
"Zai has a five-hour token window AND a weekly/monthly limit; parallel seats burn the five-hour one (5 seats ≈ 25 min, 10-11); ≤3 seats; exhausted jobs die silently; check futon3c/scripts/zai-usage."
Zai quota, as learned across projects (merged here 2026-10-12 so every project's sessions see it; minus40 relate.py found the earlier copies):
**Exhaustion is silent.** The seats share one upstream quota; when it runs out, invoke jobs end as bare `state failed` / `invoke-error` with no output, indistinguishable from a crash (voxterm memory `zai-seat-allocation`, 09-15).
**Weekly/monthly limit** is separate. 2026-09-24 it ran out ("Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted", HTTP 429, reset 09-29), stopping PROOF-2 work (voxterm memory `proof2-dispatch-pool`). The monthly meter resets around the 13th, ~02:04Z (67% used at 2026-10-12 05:15Z).
**How to apply:** run at most 3 Zai packets at once and check zai-usage before a fourth. A Zai job that comes back "done" or "failed" with nothing written may have hit a limit; check usage before re-dispatching. Related: [[wm-lean-registry-closure]] (Zai owners stall; re-audit yourself).
**Five-hour window** binds under parallel load. claude-16, 2026-10-12: five seats labelling at once exhausted it in about 25 minutes (2026-10-11 18:21Z, all jobs died on HTTP 429 having written nothing; reset 22:33Z). Two or three seats at a time was fine.
Kimi has its own five-hour window (403 on every seat when out, 09-24); don't confuse the two.
`~/code/futon3c/scripts/zai-usage` shows both Zai windows; claude-16 logs readings in futon3c `holes/labs/M-象-2000/moves/usage.log`.

Joe 2026-09-24 — reloading a shared JVM from its own master checkout never needs his permission; only a process RESTART is his call; do the reload and report it
Limit (2026-09-25): a reload only reaches code called through a var at call time. Kimi/Zai seats hold an invoke CLOSURE built by zai-api/make-invoke-fn at registration, so anything inlined in that closure body keeps its old form in every running seat until the seat is rebuilt (DELETE + POST /agents/auto) or the JVM restarts. Put seat behaviour in top-level defns called from the closure, not inline.
**How to apply:** after commits land on master in a repo on a serving JVM's classpath, reload the changed namespaces via `futon3c/scripts/proof-eval.sh` with `(require 'ns :reload)` in dependency order, verify with `scripts/wm_load_identity.sh` or a var check, and REPORT the reload. Never load a worktree or branch copy. A process restart (futon3c :6768/:7070, futon1b, API :7073, liveness-only :7072) is still Joe's call, though futon1b needs no quiet time ([[futon1b-restart-policy]]).
2026-09-27: I again wrote that I would bring a reload list to Joe "as one request". Joe: "Reloading is fine as you know, I don't need to be involved as you have Drawbridge." Do the reload through `futon3c/scripts/proof-eval.sh` and report it afterwards. What does still need him: a RESTART, including when a new jar dependency (deps.edn change) is not on the running JVM's classpath — check with `(Class/forName ...)` before assuming.
**Why:** CLAUDE.md already says "Restart of a shared JVM is Joe's call; reload-from-master is always allowed." Waiting for permission left landed code dead in the serving JVM for hours and pushed an operator decision onto Joe that was never his.
Joe, 2026-09-24: "reload does not need my permission, that is a misconception." I had been ending reports with "pending your reload".

Joe (2026-09-25) asked that each Kimi dispatch use a unique requisition ID. The mechanism is `futon3c/scripts/kimi-task.sh --from <me> --to <kimi-N> --purpose "<line>" packet.md`. It creates and commits `futon2/holes/excursions/E-kimi-task-N.md`, then bells with `Requisition: E-kimi-task-N — purpose`. README-kimi.md (as of 2026-09-25) says nothing about requisitions, so read the script and `zai_api.clj` parse-requisition rather than the README.
**How to apply:** use kimi-task.sh for every Kimi packet, not `agency_send.py --requisition "M-..."`. The script neither parks nor passes --mission, so take the job id from its output, confirm the job is running, then park in a second call. See [[kimi-seat-creation]].
Joe 2026-09-25 — every Kimi dispatch gets a unique requisition via futon3c/scripts/kimi-task.sh (E-kimi-task-N); README-kimi doesn't document it; the script doesn't park
**Why:** a Kimi seat keeps its conversation per requisition target and clears it only when the target changes. Reusing one M-* target across dispatches carries old context into new work. Because the file records who created it and for which seat (caller-minted-task?), the caller's own clock stays on its mission.
